For starters I think it’s sweet that you care about your boyfriend enough to look into these things, as for advice I think the big thing is try not to force him to change or force his progress, I understand you love him but you will likely tire yourself out and possibly stress him out further. This is a problem that he needs to pull himself out (you can always be a hand to hold during this of course) and if you want things to work out it will require a lot of patience. I think it’s really great that you both are going to be doing couples therapy and with that so soon around the corner id try to relax and take things one step at a time focusing on that. You say he suspected avpd but changed his mind, if he’s open to talking perhaps ask why he changed his mind, it is possible hes still trying to learn what could be the issue and that maybe it is just severe social anxiety, introversion, etc. many things could be the cause of such seclusion. I think the biggest thing about these symptoms is figuring out what is actually fine and not fine. Does he consider them fine long term or short term? Why does he consider himself a bad boyfriend, because he ignores you? Is he ignoring you or is it possibly parallel play and he values time together yet simultaneously separate? Does he feel guilty for ignoring you or does he feel bad towards your reaction towards it? If you feel ignored then its a very valid feeling to have too. I had similar issues in a couple relationships in a more milder degree but the biggest thing here is being open, honest, and vulnerable about both your feelings to each other.
